label: text

YANGTZE RIVER
DISASTER.

label: text
text: THRIBLE EXPLIENCE

label: text
text: The Kyodu Maru is to-day a sunken hulk on the shores of an uninhabited island off the mouth of the Yangtze, while a Japanese destroyer, bearing the Japanese Admiral and the Marine Inspector attached to the local Japanese Consulate, and a tug manned by Japanese marines, are searching the waters adjacent to the scene of the tragedy in an effort to find five Japanese officers and 25 of the crew of the ill-tated vessel, says the "Shanghai Times."

label: text
text: News of the disaster was brought a Shanghai on Sunday, when a Chinese steamer arrived carrying ve exhausted survivors of the rede, two Japanese officers and three Chinese crew members.

label: text
text: The men related how the Kyodu Maru, on her regular run between Shanghai and Dairen, somehow got out of her course and struck on the

label: text
text: Burton is the last Wednesday. The entire ship's crew handed and for several days lived off such of the vessel's stores as they were able to salvage. Then food and water ran out. Several Chinese junks passed,

label: text
text: s a based for piratical operation, he junkmen refused to go near in response to signals of distress.

label: text
text: response to signals of distress. Finally, it was decided to try and reach help with a small boat. The tiny craft was not equipped for navigating the rough waters and the quintette drifted about for 20 hours without food or water until they were picked up near Chinghai on the Chinese steamer.

label: text
text: On arrival here, the Japanese Consul-General immediately despatched Destroyer No. 5, the Admiral and Marine Inspector going along. Enter a tag was sent to the scene. Due to the refusal of Chinese to man the tag, 20 marines were sent aboard as crew.

label: text
text: Wireless messages received from the destroyer report that the Kyodu Maru is under water with her topmasts unwash. No trace of the crew could be found.

label: text
text: The fate of the crew of the vessel is in doubt, fear being entertained for their safety. It is thought possible that, unable to endure the pungs of hunger and the cravings of thirst, the entire ship's company embarked on small boats or improvised rafts in an effort to reach inhabited land or the track of the regular stemmers. Another possibility is that the island was visited by pirates shortly after the during quintette embarked on their heroic mission who either killed or carried into captivity the luckless castways.

label: text
text: Hopeless are entertained that the shipwrecked men were picked up by a friendly craft without means of communication, and are now on their way either to Shanghai or some other China port.

label: text
text: The Kyodu plied regularly between Shanghai and Dairen and was on her way to the northern port when the accident happened. She carries a crew of 28 Chinese semen and seven Japanese officers. It is believed the vessel is wrecked beyond possibilities of salvage.

1,000 MILES AWAY.

label: text
text: UNIQUE TEST SUCCEEDS

label: text
text: So amazing have been the strides made in the application of modern scientific discoveries to medical matters that it has been possible for a record of the beating of a man's heart to be thrown on a screen before a gathering of doctors many miles away. And, while watching the screen, they were able to hear a broadcast diagnosis of the case, and compare the latter with their own conclusions, drawn from what was so mysteriously displayed before them.

label: text
text: Unique test of new use for the transmission of photographs by wire was made in Chicago, New York, and Atlantic City, simultaneously and successfully.

label: text
text:
The action of a man's heart was photographed in New York, and the picture immediately transmitted by wire a thousand miles to Chicago. Here the diagnosis made by a heart expert was promptly broadcast by a physician to the Atlantic City Convention Hall, where the American Medical Association members were gathered. There 1,500 doctors compared the broadcast diagnosis with a copy, thrown on the screen, of the electro stethogram or chart of the heart beat, and the cardiogram of the heart action, taken in New York, two hrs earlier.

label: paragraph_title
text: "THE KING'S PIPE."

label: text
text: BAD TOBACCO'S FIERY END.

label: text
text: London's docks don't the champion smoker in England, writes correspondent of the "Daily Chronicles." He gets through anything up to a ton of bad tobacco a day, year in, year out, and yet is innocent of smoker's heart or throat trouble.

label: text
text: All kinds of tobacco come to him alike, and it is a matter of in- difference whether his daily ration is a million cigarettes, a cart-load of Havana cigars, or a ton of shing.

label: text
text: Under the watchful eye of a previous Customs officer he consumes whatever is given him in the 8ft. deep bowl of his pipe, and puffs out the smoke through a 10ft. chimneystack "holder" into the ablations of Victorin Dock.

label: text
text: In his m re exalted moments he esponds to the numb of the King's Pipe, but popularly is known as The Kiln, and his job is to destroy utterly all-bud or unsaleable tobacco at the Port of London Authority warehouses. floor sweepings and even cigarettes or cigars for which merchants can find no sale, but can, by passing them through the King's Pipe, recover the duty they paid.

label: paragraph_title
text: THK STOKER

label: text
text: It seems to worked waste, but there it is. Every day he smokes away tobacco which had it rained sweet and fragrant, would as worth £1,000 on the market. The Kiln's stokers have to be murtained men of wonderful self-control. The other day they shovelled several thousands of Havana eigns (beautiful to look at) into the greedy mow of the furnace without turning a hair and without surreptitious hand finding its way to a pocket. Human restraint can surely go no further.

label: text
text: They have fed it, with 400,000 Russian cigarettes, each one equipped with a paper holder. A market could not be found for them, and their fiery death in the King's Pipe has recovered for their owners the 8s, 2d, per lb. duty paid on their behalf in their earlier days of promise.

label: text
text: 'This insatiable smoker's work does not go for nothing for the tobacco he burns in the kiln supplies heat for the tobacco drying rooms in the warehouses. Thus My Lady Nicotine becomes her own handmade.

label: text
text: It comes from every country in the world where they grow tobacco. Thus you find aristocratic Dubec (Turkish) tobacco worth a sovereign a pound in its raw duty-free state, and papery rubbish from the Orient that may fetch 3d. a pound to be made into insect poison.

label: text
text: But both of them are tobacco to the unsentimental Customs official, and whether they are going to be Bond Street cigarettes or green-flies' terror, they stand on level footing when it comes to paying their 3a. 2d. a lb. duty.

label: text
text: Altogether there is about £40,000,000 worth of tobacco in the Port Authorities warehouses, of which £12,000,000 is the value of the raw material and £28,000,000 the prospective duty.

label: text
text: "There are said to be 135 varies ties of Russian tobacco alone," said Mr. J. R. H. Inkster, head of the Port of London Tobacco Department, to a "Daily Chronicle" reporter, "so there must be thousands in all."

label: text
text: "Virginian is easily first in quantity at the London Dockes, and of its kind first in quality also, although it has been imitated in many countries. Countries that have tried to grow it include England, Ireland, India, Canada, Nyasalund and Rhodesia, but there is something in the soil of Virginia that makes it impossible to equal elsewhere.

label: text
text:
However, after years of experiment, Rhodesia is successfully producing both Virginian and Turkish tobaccos, and there is a great future for the country in tobacco growing. English and Irish Virginian is hardly worth smoking.
Virginian tobacco comes to the London Docks in huge casks or bogheads weighing half a ton. There are tens of thousands of these in the warehouses, and each represents about £125 in raw tobacco and £450 in duty.

label: text
text: OREAKING CABES.

label: text
text:
For about three years the hogsheads remain in the warehouses while the tobacco matures in the wood. And they do not mature in peace. Three times a year a sort of fermentation goes on inside, causing the tobacco to swell so much that the casks tumble about in uncanny fashion. Occasionally during fermentation a pile of half-ton hogsheads in a warehouse will be thrown around in confusion as if by a ghostly giant, and in the stillness you can hear them creaking as if they were going to burst.

label: paragraph_title

PARSEE'S MURDER.
THREE MEN TO DIE.

label: text
text: Bombay

label: text
text: The notorious Malabar Hill murder case concluded at the Sessions Court, when, of the nine men accused of complicity in the murder on January 12 of Mr. A. Q. Bawla, the wealthy Parsee merchant, of Bombay, seven were found guilty and two acquitted.

label: text
text: The charges against the whole of the accused included assaults on Mumtaz Begum, a twenty-two-year-old dancing girl, and Lieut. Saegert, a British officer who was one of a party which gallantly went to the rescue when Dawla and Mumtaz Begum were attacked by the accused. Lieut. Saegert was wounded by a knife thrust.

label: text
text: Sentence of death was passed upon three of the accused, namely, Shafi Ahmed, who was a rialdar (native officer) of the Indore State-Mounted Police; Shami Rao Dighe, a captain of the Indore Air Force; and Nate Pande, a high official of the Maharajah of Indore's household. Four others, including Anand Rao Phanee, Adjutant-General of the Indore Army, were sentenced to transportation for life.

label: paragraph_title
text: NATIVE DANCES.

label: text
text: BASIS OF A NEW HEALTH SYSTEM.

label: text
text: Native dances as done by native men and women in North and South America, Australia, Africa, and other parts of the world form the basis of a new health system which a New Zealander, Mr. F. A. Hornibrook, and his wife are urging the civilised world to adopt.

label: text
text: Forty-six doctors and a number of eminent scientists attended as demonstration in London, when, after a paper read by Mrs. Hornibrook on the scientific side of the theory, a Maori from New Zealand gave examples of the original dances, and Mr. Hornibrook demonstrated exercises based on them and adapted for civilised men and women with little time to spare.

label: text
text: The strengthening of the abdominal wall is the end to which the system is adapted, and it is claimed to have exceptional results in the treatment of intestinal troubles.

label: text
text: "These native dances are really a system of physical education which, judged by its material results or judged by its hygienic effects, is far in advance of anything which the Europeans now have." Mrs. Hornibrook told a "Daily News" representative: "Yet we Europeans in our insolent conceit, suppose such dance exercises were merely grotesque antics, un-becoming gestures, without any survival-value-of-hygienic-useful-ness."

label: text
text: Modern civilised dancing is not enough." Mr. Hornbrook added. "It moves the shoulders and the legs, but the middle part of the body, the all-important part, no-missing rigid."
